name: Mediator

pf.license.what the business is: Mediation: a neutral person helps two or more people reach their own agreement. A mediator does not decide, does not give legal advice and is not either person's lawyer. Some mediators are also lawyers; the mediation stays separate from legal advice.
pf.license.need: Many places set no license for mediators. Where the state's rules require training or a roster listing for court-connected or family mediation, the mediator holds that certificate. A mediator who is also a lawyer holds their own bar license.
pf.license.ask: Optional: a training certificate, a court roster listing or a bar number, only if the business wants it shown.
pf.license.how it's checked: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, certificate, roster listing or insurance (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks going live: nothing waits on a license or certificate (D96): the business goes live once set up and the owner says yes. A job the owner says needs a certificate they don't have isn't booked.
pf.license.renewals: The owner may give end dates; Rosie reminds Sam before they pass. It looks nothing up.
pf.license.insurance: Professional liability insurance is the business's own choice; Rosie shows it only as the business gives it.

pf.services.the dispute itself: Never decided, judged or advised on by Rosie or its AI. The agreement belongs to the parties.
pf.services.capacity: One mediator per session; a co-mediator only by name. A joint session is booked after each party's intake meeting.
pf.services.online: Intake meetings and sessions by video count as at the office (flow A).
pf.services.booking window: Up to 6 weeks ahead; no same-day sessions.

pf.questions.who may book: An adult books for themselves. They add each other person by name and contact; each other person says yes on their own link and gives their own answers. Nobody books for an adult who hasn't agreed. A child is never a party.

words that stop a booking: someone is hurting or threatening a person right now

what Rosie says.abuse or fear: If you're in danger, call 911. The National Domestic Violence Hotline is 1-800-799-7233, any time. The booking goes on privately: no joint session is offered, only a meeting with the mediator alone, and Rosie asks how it's safe to reach the customer.
what Rosie says.pressured to agree: The mediator meets you alone first. Nobody has to agree to anything. The booking goes on.

pf.safety.legal questions: Never answered: whether a deal is fair, what a court would do, what the law says. A mediator who is also a lawyer keeps legal advice outside the mediation. In danger, 911 comes first.

pf.visit.check-in: At the office: the code at the front desk. By video: the mediator asks for the code at the start. At a place the parties pick: the code from the person who booked, at the door.
pf.visit.at check-in: Each person signs the agreement to mediate if they haven't. The mediator says again that they are neutral, give no legal advice and decide nothing.
pf.visit.work changes: An extra hour is priced and OK'd by every party first. A second session is its own visit. A party who wants to stop can stop at any time.
pf.visit.a conflict or a safety concern found: The mediator stops the joint session. Nothing is charged for the part not done. A private meeting with each person can come first. No reason is texted.
pf.visit.what proves it's done: The code, or DONE. The written summary, if the parties asked for one, goes to each person on their own secure page.
pf.visit.after the session: The parties decide what comes next: another session, a written summary, or an end. Rosie records only that the session happened.

pf.money.before: Intake meetings and follow-ups: nothing taken (the starting answer). A mediation session: a deposit when booked (the example: $100 of $300). A half-day mediation: paid in full when booked. At a place the parties pick: a deposit, or a card saved for the travel fee. A deposit is never more than the price, and any cap comes from the state form.
pf.money.after: At the office: the rest at the front desk, the business's own way. By video or at a place the parties pick: Rosie texts the bill, or charges the saved card at DONE. An extra hour is priced and OK'd first and paid with the rest.
pf.money.who pays: The person who books pays through Rosie. Another party can be named as the payer and gets a pay link after the session. How the parties share the cost between themselves is their own agreement, outside Rosie.
pf.money.fees: A late-cancel or no-show fee: the example keeps the deposit (or the $60 travel fee on a saved card). It's shown before booking, and Sam confirms each. A fee is never more than what was paid now.
pf.money.cancel: The example: free to cancel until 2 days before the session.
pf.money.tax: None by default; where the state's rules tax the service, the rate comes from the state form.
pf.money.rosfield: the $2 per confirmed booking applies, as to every kind of work (D97): a flat fee for each booking Rosie's AI makes, paid by the business, never added to the customer's price; a booking the business puts in itself carries no $2; card payments cost only Stripe's own card fee.

pf.messages.texts say: only the business's plain name, the date, the time and the place. Each person is texted only about their own part, and never told what another person answered.
pf.messages.safe to text: If a person says texts or email aren't safe, Rosie uses only the way they pick: the secure page, an email, or a call from the business. Any text then names only the business's plain name and the time.
pf.messages.others asking: Rosie never confirms to anyone but the customer (or a person the customer added) that a person is a customer or has a booking, including the other party before they have said yes.
pf.messages.a conflict: Never explained. No other mediator is suggested.
pf.messages.no nudges: No follow-up texts about booking another session.
pf.messages.case notes: The mediator's notes stay in the business's own file, never in Rosie. Rosie keeps only the time, the kind of dispute and that the session happened.
pf.messages.languages: English and Spanish, plus any languages the owner adds.
pf.messages.minors: A child is never a party. A teen's request goes to a parent.

pf.staff.licenses: Any certificate or listing is shown as the business gives it; Rosie doesn't check it.
pf.staff.supervision: An office manager may run the desk and the neutrality check, but never mediates and never gives advice.
pf.staff.who OKs what: The neutrality check: the mediator named or Sam. Sam OKs prices made for one customer. Sam's answer wins.
pf.staff.stand-ins: Only another mediator at the same business, offered by the business and picked by the customer by name. Rosie never suggests one. Nobody moves on silence.

pf.rules.neutral: The mediator is neutral. They never take a side, never decide, and never give legal advice. They are not any party's lawyer.
pf.rules.notice at booking: The mediator is neutral, gives no legal advice and decides nothing. Each person may have a lawyer of their own. Before the party form clears, share only names and the kind of dispute.
pf.rules.voluntary: Every party agrees on their own page. Nobody is booked into a mediation they haven't said yes to. Any party may stop at any time.
pf.rules.safety: Where a party says they fear the other, no joint session is booked. The mediator meets each person alone, or the business declines. This is the business's own screening; Rosie only routes the booking privately.
pf.rules.confidentiality: What is said in a session stays in the session as the signed agreement says, except what the law requires. Rosie never sees it.
pf.rules.named only: Rosie books only a mediator or business the customer names. It never suggests, ranks or rates mediators, and sends no rating request.
pf.rules.records: Booking records 7 years. The mediator's notes stay in the business's own system.
pf.rules.status: Draft: finalized once the state forms are filled in.

matter most.one party says yes, the other doesn't: Nothing is booked for a joint session until every party has said yes on their own link; the first person's intake meeting can still go ahead.
matter most.fear of the other person: Safety steps first. No joint session; a private meeting with the mediator, or the business declines.
matter most.a protective order: No joint session is booked. The mediator decides what, if anything, can be offered.
matter most.a conflict: Told without the reason; nothing owed; no other mediator suggested.
matter most.a legal question by text: Never answered; it waits for a lawyer of their own.
matter most.texts aren't safe: Only the way the customer picks; plain texts with no matter.
matter most.a party asks what the other said: Never told. Each person's answers stay on their own page.
matter most.a child as a party: Not booked. A teen's request goes to a parent.
matter most.the session can't start (a party missing: Nothing is charged for the part not done; the deposit goes back unless the missing party's choice is the business's fee rule.
matter most.a no-show: The fee the business set and the customer agreed to; Sam confirms each.

pf.edges.the rest: All other edge cases are handled the generic way.

notes:
New work, built Tue Oct 27 2026 (REDESIGN 2 master, N3b) from the lawyer overlay ("from": "lawyer"); there is no sample, no test-drive and no old flowchart for a mediator, so every price, fee and rule below is the example business's own, not a standard. The lawyer's conflict check becomes a neutrality check on the party form (names only), the lawyer's named-only rule stays, and the lawyer's trust-account money rule is dropped (a mediator takes ordinary deposits).
A mediation has two or more people. One books; every other person is added by name and contact, says yes on their own link, signs the agreement to mediate, and gives their own answers (the master's "each signs their own form on their own link"). Nobody sees another person's answers. A child is never a party (A4-24 and B4-32 "A child" branches off). How the people share the cost is their own agreement outside Rosie.
Safety: danger first (911, 988, the family-violence hotline). Fear of the other person or a protective order: safety steps, the booking is made private on their word (D74), no joint session is offered, only a meeting with the mediator alone, or the business declines. Rosie only routes it; the screening is the business's own. Pressed to agree: the mediator meets you alone first.
Licenses and certificates are optional and never checked by Rosie (D96); pf.license says so. A mediator who is also a lawyer keeps legal advice outside the mediation. Rosie never gives legal advice (S13-04 more; A3-26 / B3-21 words; A7-12 / B7-16 more).
Prices (examples): intake meeting $75 a person; mediation session (2 hours) $300 with a $100 deposit and a $200 rest; half-day mediation (4 hours) $550 paid in full; extra hour $120; follow-up session $150. At a place the parties pick: $360 = the $300 session plus a $60 travel fee (one price, so the bill adds up); $120 deposit and $240 rest, or a card saved for the $60 fee; a half-day at a workplace $660 = $600 plus the $60, paid in full.
Money paths. A: list|deposit|counter (main), list|full|none, list|none|bill. B: list|deposit|bill (main), list|card|card, list|full|none. Each path has its own amounts row (price, deposit and rest or paid, fee, name); every fee is no more than what was paid now; no hold; the rest is paid at the visit or on the bill. money.A.services: Intake meeting ($75, card saved, counter), Half-day mediation ($550, paid in full); money.B.services: Second intake meeting at your location ($75, card saved, card at DONE), Half-day mediation at a workplace ($660, paid in full). The $2 applies (D97): S1-62's "No $2" branch is off.
Switch sensitive (private disputes: no matter or service name in a text, no rating). Facts: forms (the party form), firststeps (an intake meeting before a joint session), documents (the agreement to mediate, signed by every person: A5-19), video, extrawork. Settings: arrive set start (both flows), cutoff 2 days before.
Rename: the lawyer's pairs re-pointed (office Lee Mediation, 52 Grove St, mediators Dana Reyes and Omar Hassan; on-site Lee On-Site Mediation, 715 Harbor Rd, mediators Noor Khan and Felix Brandt; customer location 18 Birch Ln); master numbers mapped by role (the haircut is the mediation session, the groom's package the full-day mediation, the signature cut the half-day mediation); license numbers in the master examples shown as EX-1042 style. Pairs protect master sentences that use the word "cut" in other senses.
Off: sent-now, seats, spaces, stays, classes, photo quotes, walk-ins, a drop-off, a child left or a child party, "nobody home", an estimate that becomes a staged job, someone in care missing, ratings. Own steps: none. Detail lines (more) for the plug-in: S1-11, S13-04, S13-07, S13-20, A3-22 / B3-17, A4-43 / B4-38, A4-26 / B4-27, A7-12 / B7-16, A8-51; words ops for the legal-question reply (A3-26, B3-21) and the sign-up money read-backs (S1-13).
Not sure (for the verifier): the sign-up card keeps the master's nine rows, so some rows are example services (Phone check-in, Separate-room mediation, Agreement write-up, Free intro call) with example prices; the deposit amount ($100 of $300) and the 2-day cutoff are examples; where the deposit falls against the neutrality check (the master takes money at its own money step; I did not force the check before it); the master's B4-100 line "only the person the visit is for, or their legal guardian, can book this" reads against "one person books for the group".
